[Wed 2026-04-08 17:33 UTC] You are given a broad information-seeking task that requires collecting and organizing information into a structured table format.

### Query
Could you help compile a detailed dataset of Eileen Gu's competitive achievements in freestyle skiing from Jan, 2015 to Jan 31st 2025, including the following information: event dates (year and month), specific event names (e.g., Winter Olympic Games, FIS Freestyle Ski World Championships, FIS Freestyle Ski World Cup stops, Winter Youth Olympic Games, X Games), event levels (e.g., Olympic, World Championship, World Cup, Youth Olympic, invitational, etc.), disciplines (women's big air, women's slopestyle, women's halfpipe, etc.), and results (e.g., gold medal, the 4th, etc.), and the top 3 players? By the way, as for competitions, only official matches should be counted, preliminary qualifiers should not be included.

Please organize the results in one Markdown table with the following columns:
Date, Event Name,  Level, Discipline, Result, Top 3 Players

Don't ask me any questions, just output the results according to the columns without omitting cells arbitrarily. The output format is a markdown code block.

### Output Requirements
- **Format**: Markdown table wrapped in triple backticks with markdown specifier
- **Required Columns** (6): date, eventname, level, discipline, result, top3players
- **Unique Key Columns**: date, discipline, eventname
- **Expected Rows**: 58 rows

**IMPORTANT**: Write the markdown table to `answer.txt` in the workspace.

**IMPORTANT**: You must NOT read the `ground_truth.csv` file in the workspace. Use web search to find all information.

**Note**: You may use available tools or skills in the system to complete this task.

and you need to complete the task in 480s.

## What are Eileen Gu’s career highlights in freeskiing?

Gu’s career highlights stretch back to her youth career, when she quickly rose to the top of the rankings. She earned her maiden World Cup victory in 2019 and grabbed two Youth Olympic medals in 2020. In her first X Games appearance, she won medals in all three of her events, including a pair of gold medals in slopestyle and superpipe. A pair of world championship titles and her three Olympic medals cap off an impressive résumé for the 22-year-old.

## How many X Games medals has Eileen Gu won?

Gu has won medals in four out of five X Games competitions she’s entered. At her X Games debut in 2021, Gu won gold in superpipe and slopestyle and took home bronze in big air. Gu did not return to the X Games until 2024, when she won the superpipe for the second time. She did compete at the 2025 X Games, but a fall during the streetstyle event had her finishing off the podium in fourth place and forced her to pull out of the other events.

## What are Eileen Gu’s World Cup results?

Gu has been dominant on the World Cup circuit since the 2022 Beijing Olympics. In her 12 appearances, she has 10 wins and two runner-up finishes. Although Gu primarily has competed in halfpipe competitions, she also logged a slopestyle victory at last season’s Laax Open.

## What signature tricks is Eileen Gu known for?

While Gu has a loaded roster of tricks up her sleeve, there are several tricks that have become synonymous with her career. She was the first woman to land a double cork 1440 in a freeski competition and later landed a double cork 1620 during her first-ever attempt, which came during the Olympic big air final in 2022. Additionally, Gu often includes a rightside cork 900 with a Buick grab in her halfpipe and slopestyle runs.

## Has Eileen Gu set any records?

At Beijing 2022, Gu set the record as freestyle skiing’s youngest Olympic champion (18) and made history as the first athlete to win three freestyle skiing medals at a single Olympic Games. She also was the first woman in history to win three medals at their X Games debut.

## What impact has Eileen Gu had on women’s freeskiing?

Gu’s impact on freeskiing is immeasurable. Her performance at the 2022 Beijing Olympics catapulted her into global stardom, a platform she has continued to grow and leverage in the four years since. On the snow, she has pushed both the definition of success and the physical limits of the sport to new heights. In China, a recent surge of popularity in skiing has been credited to Gu’s success.

## Will Eileen Gu compete at the 2026 Milan Cortina Olympics?

The qualification period for freeskiing still is ongoing, but barring injury, Gu is a predicted lock to represent China at the 2026 Winter Games.

## What events will Eileen Gu ski in at the 2026 Milan Cortina Olympics?

Gu primarily has competed in halfpipe competitions since the 2022 Olympics but remains a wildcard for both the slopestyle and big air competitions. Multiple factors, including injury recovery, could affect Gu’s decision at the 2026 Winter Games.

## How is Eileen Gu recovering from her 2025 training injury before Milan Cortina?

Gu suffered an injury in August 2025 while training in New Zealand. The injury occurred just as Gu was getting back to on-snow training after previously injuring her shoulder. While Gu has not publicly commented on her status, she posted videos of herself looking strong, skiing as recently as Sept. 18. 

## What is Eileen Gu's medal outlook for Milan Cortina 2026?

Gu has looked indomitable in halfpipe competitions since 2022, making her an early favorite to defend her gold at the Milan Cortina Games. Although she’s only competed in two World Cup slopestyle events since the last Olympics, she finished on the podium both times. If Gu competes in all three events, another history-making effort certainly is possible.

Since the Beijing Olympics, Gu has taken considerable time away from skiing to focus on her academics and recover from various injuries. She will need to ensure she is in peak condition come February, but it should be hard to beat her if that's the case.

Now this is getting interesting. Another sensational teen from California making noise on the FIS World Cup circuit? Yes, it’s Eileen Gu, the 15-year-old San Francisco sensation!

After winning her first World Cup medal – a silver – on 12 January in Font Romeu (FRA), she claimed her first World Cup win with a final-round performance in Seiser Alm (ITA). Standing fourth going into the final round, she produced an excellent ride and was rewarded with a score of 84.40 that held up for the victory.

“I’m still buzzing from winning today,” said Gu afterwards. “Coming into the final run of three after messing up my first two definitely wasn’t easy, especially after qualifying first into finals. I just tried to focus on the little things in my run and it looks like it paid off! When I received my score I was astounded and ecstatic to get my first World Cup win. Not to mention, being able to share the podium with Julia made it even better.”

Megan Oldham of Canada, who took the first-round lead at 83.00, finished second and American Julia Krass finished third with her second-round run that scored 77.30. It’s Krass’s first-ever World Cup medal, after six years on the tour.

“Super happy to grab third today,” said Krass, 21. “It was a really sick week here. The course was really fun, and training went well all week. Unfortunately, I couldn’t put together the run I was hoping for today, but still so happy to land and snag third place. Everyone crushed it the whole week, especially Eileen and Megan!”

Canada’s Max Moffatt won the men’s Slopestyle, ahead of Sweden’s Oliwer Magnusson and another new American medalist, Kiernan Fagan, 17, who scored his first career World Cup medal as well.

In Mont Tremblant, Canada’s Mikael Kingsbury got back to winning in the men’s Moguls competition for his 54th career win. France’s Perrine Laffont won for the second time this season in the women’s Moguls and has now won a medal in all five events this season.

At the U.S. Aerials Championships at Lake Placid, New York, Chris Lillis and Winter Vinecki won the national titles. Lillis finished ahead of his brother, Jon Lillis, and Nick Novak in the men’s division; Madison Varmette and Kaila Kuhn went 2-3 for the women.

Both Chris Lillis and Vinecki were coming back from injuries. Said Vinecki, “It feels amazing to land some nice jumps when it counts! Becoming the U.S. National Champion is a huge confidence boost for the rest of the season to come! It is even more rewarding though because this event is almost exactly one year since my ACL surgery. Being able to come back strong with a start to my best season yet makes all the hard work worth it!”
